report:
Reviewed the complete identity_minting claim and all ten ordinary implementation entries, including the newly associated minting and reopening sites. Requirements are (1) a single owning query for each generic parameter or associated definition, (2) dependents reuse those identities, and (3) names or positions do not replace semantic handles. The referenced architectural identity-family definition distinguishes kind-specific definition symbols from GenericParam, owner/index fields, and body-local identities; it does not require every IR node to be an erased Symbol.

CheckGenerics in cst/generics.rs allocates each explicit type, lifetime, or const AstGenericParam while its owner's tracked signature executes, using owner and parameter index. generic_param.rs makes spans tracked facts and retains parent/index in the identity. structs.rs::sig, enums.rs::sig, impls.rs::sig and fns.rs::sig are the respective owning signature boundaries. traits.rs::sig owns explicit parameters and the single distinguished Self parameter, then returns both in its binder. The fns.rs signature opens the trait/impl signature, copies existing generic handles and Self type, and mints only method-level parameters; its body obtains the same signature and brings its existing handles into scope. structs.rs::fields likewise uses self.sig().iter_symbols(). The captured BinderExt implementation copies handles from the binder's stored slice; captured Ribs::add_generic_params associates existing GenericParam values with lookup names without allocating replacements. Thus using a name to find an existing handle is distinct from minting an identity from the name.

For associated functions, types and constants, associated.rs::local_trait_associated_item and local_impl_associated_item are the tracked owner/key minting boundaries. Both membership enumeration and checked member-list lowering call these same queries. Their shared lower_item constructs the appropriate symbol only within that query; keys distinguish kind, name and same-kind/name occurrence under the owner. The member list's binder copies owner generics. impls.rs associated-type-value lookup also requests the keyed item and reuses the impl signature's generics. These are identity references rather than a second construction in each consumer. Empty generic lists, separate owners sharing parameter names, trait Self, method-level generics, and duplicate associated names are accounted for structurally by the captured paths; edit stability remains explicitly unverified by tests.

The complete associated test set consists only of sage_meta::todo::checking_identity_minting. Its body has no assertions and is not behavioral evidence. Its explicit deferred matrix requires cross-query and persistent-edit comparisons of owner, generic, Self and associated-item identities across signatures, details and bodies, including shadowed equal names. Accept this as deferred verification, not as an implemented or passing identity test: completion requires source-driven persistent-database fixtures exposing actual identity handles at those boundaries, plus assertions comparing reuse and separation before and after edits. No N/A entries exist. No behavioral violation was identified during this source inspection, and no semantic test was executed for this review. Ran cargo fmt and cargo build; build passed with warnings. Review start/read commands captured current inputs after association-only edits. Central coordinator owns required post-codegen and Sage sanity checks for these comment changes.
